longQuestions: Design of an experiment is the plan of conducting an experiment: deciding the treatments, the experimental units, the number of replications and the way treatments are allotted to units, and the method of analysis, so that valid and efficient conclusions can be drawn with minimum experimental error.
i. Experimental material — the material on which the experiment is performed (land, animals, plants, patients).
ii. Experimental unit — the smallest division of the material to which a treatment is applied (a plot, an animal).
iii. Treatment — the factor or method whose effect is studied (fertiliser, variety, drug).
iv. Uniformity trial — an experiment in which the same treatment is applied to all units to study the natural variability of the material.
v. Block — a group of homogeneous experimental units.
Randomization — allotting treatments to experimental units by a random process so that each unit has an equal chance; it removes bias and makes the error estimate valid.
Replication — repeating each treatment on more than one unit; it gives an estimate of experimental error and increases precision.
Local control — grouping homogeneous units into blocks so that variation between blocks is removed from the error, making the design more efficient.
i. Experimental design is the plan for conducting an experiment — choice of treatments, units, replication and allocation — to obtain valid conclusions with minimum error.
ii. Basic principles: randomization, replication and local control.
(a) Extraneous factors — factors other than the treatments that may affect the response (soil fertility, temperature, age of animals); they should be controlled.
(b) Experimental error — the variation among units receiving the same treatment, caused by extraneous factors and uncontrolled variation; it is estimated through replication.

Planning is needed so that the experiment answers the questions asked, with minimum cost, time and effort; it ensures that treatments are compared fairly, experimental error is estimated and reduced, bias is avoided by randomization, and the data can be analysed correctly (by ANOVA) to draw reliable conclusions.
A completely randomized design (CRD) is one in which treatments are allotted to experimental units completely at random; it is used when units are homogeneous.
Merits: simple to plan and analyse; any number of treatments and replications can be used; maximum error degrees of freedom; missing observations cause no serious problem.
Demerits: suitable only for homogeneous material; less efficient when units vary, because all variation goes into the error.
Treatments A, B, C, each replicated 5 times on 15 plots.
Number the plots 1 to 15. Using a random number table (or lottery), select 5 plots for treatment A, then 5 of the remaining for B, and the last 5 get C.
Example layout (plot: treatment): 1-B, 2-A, 3-C, 4-A, 5-B, 6-C, 7-C, 8-A, 9-B, 10-A, 11-C, 12-B, 13-A, 14-C, 15-B. ANOVA: total d.f. 14, treatments 2, error 12.

Analysis of variance (ANOVA) is a technique, developed by R. A. Fisher, for splitting the total variation in data into components due to different sources (treatments and error) and testing, by an F-test, whether several population means are equal. The F ratio = MS(treatments)/MS(error) is compared with the table value.
ANOVA is the method of partitioning total variation into variation between groups (treatments) and within groups (error) to test the equality of several means.
Assumptions: (1) observations are independent and random; (2) each population is normally distributed; (3) the populations have equal variances (homogeneity); (4) effects are additive.
i. Variance among samples (between treatments) — variation of sample means about the grand mean, SS_B = Σ nᵢ(x̄ᵢ − x̄)².
ii. Variance within samples (error) — variation of observations about their own sample means, SS_W = ΣΣ(xᵢⱼ − x̄ᵢ)².
iii. Total variation — variation of all observations about the grand mean, SS_T = ΣΣ(xᵢⱼ − x̄)² = SS_B + SS_W.
ANOVA: Treatments d.f. 2, MS = 4; Error d.f. 9, MS = 14.44; F = 4/14.44 = 0.28.
F₀.₀₅(2, 9) = 4.26; since 0.28 < 4.26, H₀ is not rejected — the three population means can be taken as equal.
